flagged.evidence: For the identity morphism of P^1_k and y the generic point, f^{-1}(y)={η}, which is not a closed subset or a set of closed points. The cited dependency, lem-curve-closed-subsets-finite, states only that “every proper closed subset Z⊊X is a finite set of closed points.” Step 3.1 asserts closedness for every y and applies that result to the generic fiber, so it does not establish finite fibers or quasi-finiteness there.

The cited dependency def-finite-morphism-schemes defines finiteness by requiring “for every affine open U=Spec A⊂S, its inverse image is affine, f^{-1}(U)=Spec B, and the induced A-algebra B is module-finite over A.” Step 3.2 invokes this criterion to assert that f^{-1}(Spec A) is affine with B finite over A before Step 5.1 establishes that f is finite. The definition does not license that inference from properness; using it here is circular and leaves the subsequent function-field finiteness argument unsupported.
